skills.trigger: When evaluating serial chest radiographs to determine the trajectory of pulmonary disease (progression vs. resolution) and characterize the nature of worsening opacities.
steps: Compare the density and distribution of lung opacities between the baseline and follow-up images, specifically noting if hazy interstitial markings have evolved into dense, confluent consolidations.
Assess the zonal distribution to confirm if the disease process remains bilateral and predominantly affects the lower lung zones or bases.

Distinguish rapid progression of diffuse airspace disease (suggestive of acute lung injury patterns like alveolar hemorrhage or ARDS) from alternatives such as resolution (clearing opacities), bacterial superinfection (new discrete nodules/cavities), or isolated pleural effusions (blunted costophrenic angles without parenchymal consolidation).
